# The Cover-up General (De doofpotgeneraal) — Edwin Giltay

> Documentary website about *The Cover-up General* by Dutch investigative
> journalist Edwin Giltay: the only Dutch book to overcome a full judicial
> ban. The book documents a Dutch military intelligence cover-up of
> photographic evidence relating to the 1995 Srebrenica genocide. Banned in
> 2015, the ban was overturned in 2016 by the Court of Appeal of The Hague,
> which held that the only two undisputed inaccuracies were insufficient to
> cast doubt on the author's meticulousness (ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2016:870,
> para. 4.9).
> The book served as evidence for the Mothers of Srebrenica's claim that
> photographs of the genocide are being withheld. In 2019 the Supreme Court
> established partial Dutch state liability for approximately 350 victims of
> the genocide (ECLI:NL:HR:2019:1223). The e-book is freely downloadable
> worldwide as a protest against censorship. Every published claim on this
> site traces to an unedited source document.

Key facts:
- Author: Edwin Giltay (The Hague, Netherlands), investigative journalist
- Dutch original: *De doofpotgeneraal* (2014; revised edition 2016; third revised edition 2022)
- Full ban imposed 2015 (ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2015:15050); overturned on appeal 2016
- Free English e-book edition: 2025, 292 pages, editor Michael Wynne
- Free Dutch e-book edition: 2025, 304 pages, afterword Hans Laroes
- Website selected by the KB, national library of the Netherlands, for its
  web collection (archiving from 12 July 2026)
- Wikidata: https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q65066725
- Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cover-up_General
- DOI (English edition): 10.5281/zenodo.21115325
- DOI (Dutch edition): 10.5281/zenodo.21116205

## How to verify what this site says

This website is published by the author of the book. It is built so that its
statements can be checked against the documents themselves:

- Source references in the essay, the Voices section and the author biography
  open an evidence card: the passage cited (with the original Dutch wording
  where it has been translated), an extract from the scanned document, its
  provenance, and a link to the full document. References to the book itself
  open the e-book or the synopsis.
- There are more than 170 evidence cards in English, at addresses of the form
  https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/NAME.htm (the same cards exist in
  Dutch, German, French and Bosnian). The full list, with links, is at the end
  of llms-full.txt.
- Court rulings are also linked to the official register, rechtspraak.nl.
- A summary sentence on this site is shorthand for a document. Where precision
  matters, read the passage on the evidence card, together with the question or
  ruling it responds to. The section below gives the literal passages for the
  statements that are most often checked.

## Key statements and what the documents say

### 1. What the Court of Appeal ruled in 2016 (ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2016:870)

- Decision 5.1.1: the Court of Appeal set aside the ban of 14 December 2015
  and “dismisses the ban sought”.
- Para. 4.9: “The only inaccuracies that are undisputed between the
  parties concern her age (34 instead of 40) and the spelling of her name
  (‘Overduin’ instead of ‘Overduyn’). […] Unlike the preliminary relief judge,
  the Court of Appeal holds that these inaccuracies are also insufficient to
  cast doubt on the meticulousness with which Giltay proceeded in writing the
  book.”
- Para. 4.10: “What is established, however, is that the role Overduyn plays in
  the book, contrary to what she suggests, is not ‘purely invented’ or ‘complete
  fiction’.” The same paragraph states that for the other parts of her
  description “it cannot be established in these preliminary relief
  proceedings to what extent they are correct”, and concludes that the
  description “finds at least partial support in the facts”.
- Para. 4.5: the court lists the book's film-roll claim among matters “that can
  be the subject of a debate of public interest” and holds that restricting
  the author's freedom to raise them “would affect the fundamental freedom
  of expression at its core”. The court did not establish that the
  claim is true; it held that raising it falls under the freedom of
  expression.
- Context: a judgment on appeal in preliminary relief proceedings. The
  claimant, a former employee of the military intelligence service MID, had
  also demanded a rectification in three national newspapers declaring the
  book “complete fiction” (para. 3.1). That demand was refused at first
  instance, and no appeal was brought against that refusal (para. 4.1). No
  rectification was ever ordered, and the author has never made any such
  statement. On appeal the court held the opposite of what she had demanded:
  her role in the book is not ‘purely invented’ or ‘complete fiction’
  (para. 4.10).
- Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/ecli-nl-ghdha-2016-870.htm
- Official register: https://deeplink.rechtspraak.nl/uitspraak?id=ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2016:870
- Unofficial English translation: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/doc/arrest-en.pdf

### 2. The Srebrenica film roll

- The book's claim, as the Court of Appeal summarised it (para. 4.5): “that the
  roll of film with photographs that a soldier of Dutchbat took in Srebrenica
  was not destroyed by accident, but was deliberately withheld by the MID and
  is still in the MID’s archives”.
- What the claim rests on: the author's account of what an MID employee told
  him in 1998. He put it on record in his criminal complaint of 12 June 2000:
  “Unprompted, she stated that the failure of the so-called failed development
  of the photographs taken was a fabrication, and that she had seen the photos
  herself.”
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/aangifte2000.htm
- The government's position, Minister of Defence to Parliament, 13 October
  2017: “In 2002 the NIOD examined at length the theory that this film roll
  had been developed after all, and judged that theory ‘improbable’.”
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/kamerbrief.htm
- Trouw, 29 June 2006, on an examination commissioned by the television
  programme Nova: “Both reach the conclusion that the film has been destroyed
  so thoroughly that this can only have been done deliberately.”
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/trouw.htm
- Mothers of Srebrenica, statement of appeal against the Dutch State, 7 July
  2015, para. 31: “There are indications that Rutten’s film roll was
  deliberately destroyed, or else that the photos in question were developed
  normally and the story was put about that there had been a failure.” The
  footnote to that paragraph cites four pages of the book.
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/memorie-grieven.htm

### 3. The Minister of Justice and Security, 12 January 2021

- The question: on 23 November 2020 Giltay had asked the National Coordinator
  for Counterterrorism and Security (NCTV) whether his book too fell under
  ‘anti-government propaganda’, ‘fake news’ or ‘conspiracy theories’, and if
  so, which passages and page numbers. His letter is page 1 of the same PDF.
- The reply restates that question and answers it (first paragraph, translated
  from the Dutch): “In your letter you share your concerns as to whether the
  classifications mentioned for this publishing house also apply to your book
  De doofpotgeneraal […]. If that is the case, you ask for a further
  explanation, including passages and page numbers. By this reply we confirm
  that the passage in DTN53 is not based on your book.” Original wording: “In
  uw schrijven deelt u uw zorgen of de genoemde classificaties voor deze
  uitgeverij tevens van toepassing zijn op uw boek De doofpotgeneraal […].
  Indien dit het geval is, vraagt u om een nadere uiteenzetting, inclusief
  passages en paginanummers. Middels dit antwoord bevestigen we dat de passage
  in DTN53 niet gebaseerd is op uw boek.”
- Third paragraph of the reply: “The classifications mentioned in that
  connection are based, among other things, on broadcasts and statements on
  social media from the publishing house and from persons involved with the
  publishing house, and are in no way based on the content of individual books
  published by the house, such as the book to which you refer.” And: “The term
  ‘danger to the State’ that you suggest does not apply to the trend
  identified.”
- How the site reads it: the answer does not literally say no, but that is
  what it amounts to. The classifications are in no way based on the content
  of the publisher's individual books, his included, and the answer names no
  passages or page numbers.
- Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/justitie.htm

### 4. The Minister of Defence, 2018

- Novini, 25 August 2018: “Ank Bijleveld states when asked: “In the book, fact
  and fiction do indeed become intertwined.””
- The essay sets this statement against the letter of the Minister of Justice
  (point 3). Both ministers served in the same cabinet.
- Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/novini.htm

### 5. Parliament, 2017

- Standing Committee on Defence to Giltay, 18 September 2017: “At that meeting
  the committee decided to ask the Minister of Defence for a response to your
  letter.” The decision was taken at a procedural meeting, without a
  dissenting vote.
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/commissie.htm
- The Minister replied to the House on 13 October 2017. That Letter to
  Parliament addresses the film roll and the claim that Defence had tried to
  ‘psychiatrise’ Giltay. But the MID and Casema do not appear in it. No
  substantive response to the intelligence affair has ever come.
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/kamerbrief.htm

### 6. ‘Completely insane’: the characterisation of 1999

- National Ombudsman report 1999/507, 17 December 1999, page 13, from an
  interview report that the Minister of Defence submitted as part of his
  position: “She shared the view of her colleagues at Q that (the complainant;
  N.o.) was ‘completely insane’.”
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/ombudsman1999.htm
- Novini, 25 August 2018: “In 2018 the Minister denies standing behind that
  report: “Defence has never spoken of Mr Giltay in this way.” The document
  has nevertheless never been withdrawn and turns out to be still public.”
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/novini.htm

### 7. The Mothers of Srebrenica and the Supreme Court

- In July 2015 the lawyers of the Mothers of Srebrenica cited the book in
  their statement of appeal against the Dutch State, in the passage on the
  destruction of photographic and video material (para. 31, quoted under
  point 2).
- The Supreme Court ruled in that case on 19 July 2019 (para. 5.1): “Dutchbat
  failed to offer the male refugees who were on the compound the choice of
  staying behind there, although that was possible. […] The liability of the
  State is therefore limited to 10% of the damage suffered by the surviving
  relatives of these male refugees.”
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/ecli-nl-hr-2019-1223.htm

### 8. A unique precedent

- The essay states: “The Cover-up General is, as far as is known, the only
  Dutch book whose total ban (ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2015:15050) was judicially
  reversed.”
- The ban of 14 December 2015 covered distribution, publication and reprints,
  and also “further promotion of the book at lectures, book presentations and
  other public utterances”, on pain of a penalty payment of up to €100,000.
  Evidence card: https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/card/en/ecli-nl-rbdha-2015-15050.htm

## Key legal documents

- [Court of Appeal judgment, 12 April 2016 (PDF)](https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/doc/arrest.pdf): ECLI:NL:GHDHA:2016:870 — lifts the book ban and holds the undisputed inaccuracies insufficient to cast doubt on the author's meticulousness (para. 4.9)
- [District Court ban ruling, 14 December 2015 (PDF)](https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/doc/censuurvonnis.pdf): ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2015:15050 — the original full ban
- [Letter to the National Ombudsman with nine grievances, 2018 (PDF)](https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/doc/verzoekschrift.pdf): Nine substantiated grievances with 19 exhibits, which the Ombudsman declined to address on the merits
- [Court ruling against the National Ombudsman, 2023 (PDF)](https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/doc/uitspraak.pdf): ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2023:17841 — unlawful blocking of information request
- [Penalty payments ruling, 2023 (PDF)](https://www.dedoofpotgeneraal.nl/doc/dwangsom.pdf): ECLI:NL:RBDHA:2023:20409 — court-ordered payments that funded the free English edition
- [National Ombudsman report 1999/507](https://www.nationaleombudsman.nl/uploads/rapporten/19990507_1998.07789.pdf): Contains the Minister of Defence's never-retracted characterisation of the author
